messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acmehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Key management and SOC 2 questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo this morning — it was helpful to see Redwood's routing and fallback behavior. A few items we flagged on our side and I wanted to capture them here so we can drive next steps: 

1) SOC 2 status: can you confirm if Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and the expected date for the next audit report? Our procurement team needs the exact scope (hosted API vs private deployments).

2) KMS / BYOK options: we heard you support customer-managed keys in Private mode — can you outline the concrete options (cloud KMS integrations vs external HSM)? Do you support HSM-backed key import (PKCS#11) for on-prem HSMs?

3) In-transit vs at-rest: please confirm what is encrypted by default for hosted vs private (e.g., object storage, KV cache snapshots, logs). We also need a statement on whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext when customers bring their own keys.

4) Audit / evidence: our security team asked for redaction/PII controls in logs and audit log retention policy.

I've attached Acme's short vendor security questionnaire (PDF) — if you could start that and point us to any existing artifacts (SOC 2 report, encryption whitepaper, KMS design doc) that would be great.

Looking to schedule a technical workshop next week with our infra/security leads to deep-dive on BYOK and HSM proof. Availability: Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks,
Tom

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Key management and SOC 2 questions

Tom — thanks, appreciate the clear list. Recapping and answering at a high level here so the security team has a starting point; Rishi (Product Security) and Lauren (Solutions) are looped to follow with technical artifacts.

Quick answers / clarifications: 
- SOC 2: Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II covering the hosted inference control plane and customer data processing for the Hosted API. Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) are covered for the control plane we manage; customer-managed infrastructure elements and on-prem HSMs are scoped to the customer's audit. We can provide the latest SOC 2 report via NDA / secure link.

- BYOK & HSM: In Private mode we support several patterns:
  • Cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) with envelope encryption.
  • HSM-backed keys: we support Cloud HSM for managed HSM-backed keys and have a PKCS#11-compatible connector for on-prem HSMs (customer handles HSM provisioning and we interface via a secure tunnel).
  • Key rotation and policy: rotation can be handled via KMS policies or ad-hoc rotation — we track key IDs and publish key-rotation events to the audit log.

- Access to plaintext: For Hosted API we process plaintext in memory inside our secured runtime (SOC 2 controls apply). For Private / customer-managed key deployments, Redwood's runtime never has access to the raw key material — we operate with wrapped keys and the customer HSM/KMS performs unwrap operations locally (we can provide an architecture diagram).

- Logs & redaction: We offer configurable log redaction and tokenization for request/response logging. Audit logs are retained per contract; default retention is 90 days for hosted, adjustable for enterprise.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We (Redwood) will start the vendor questionnaire and return answers + attachments (SOC 2 link, encryption primer).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical workshop with Rishi and your infra/security team to walk the PKCS#11 connector and key lifecycle (Tue/Wed mornings PT work for us).
3) Confirm whether you need a HIPAA BAA — we can pass legal's standard BAA and timing depends on contract cadence.

I've attached a short "Redwood Crypto Primer" (one-pager) that explains the BYOK patterns and data flow. Rishi will follow with the deeper design documentation and a proposed workshop agenda.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Tom — great questions. Quick confirmations and attachments we'll deliver before the workshop: 

- Network: the PKCS#11 connector supports mutual-TLS over a customer-initiated tunnel (we can also operate over site-to-site VPN where required). We'll include a network topology diagram showing both options.

- Crypto specifics: envelope encryption uses AES-256-GCM for payloads, with RSA-3072 for key-wrapping in legacy/interop modes. We'll attach the crypto spec and a short rotation-policy summary (default rotation cadence: 90 days, configurable).

- Artifacts & checklist: Rishi will drop the following into the secure HubSpot folder before the workshop: SOC 2 report (access-controlled link), architecture diagram for BYOK flows, PKCS#11 connector guide, HSM attestation guidance, and a one-page procurement/security checklist.

Workshop — we can do Wed 12/22 09:00am PT. Rishi will send the calendar invite (link included below). Please confirm attendee list (we recommend infra + security + procurement).

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.
